sections.label: Reasons for repealing section 377A
sections.summary: The speaker says he explained the reasons for repealing section 377A in the debate on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In the debate we have just had on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill, I have explained the reasons for repealing section 377A.

sections.label: Risk to democratic value of Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker says it is untrue that Parliament's democratic value could be diluted if Singaporeans' views are not adequately ventilated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Given the very public opinion on the impending repeal of section 377A, there is a risk that the democratic value of the Parliament could be diluted if the views of Singaporeans on the subject are not adequately ventilated in the House." That is the point I was responding to and that is simply untrue.

sections.label: Whip and free voting
sections.summary: The speaker says not lifting the whip would deny Workers' Party MPs not in favour of repeal the chance to vote freely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If needed, I can read out other paragraphs, but I think I am just reading out what he said.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But immediately after that, also, I said "not lifting the whip would deny Workers' Party Members of Parliament (MPs) not in favour of a repeal of section 377A the opportunity to vote freely and in doing so, to also represent Singaporeans who see this issue as a matter of deep religious belief and conscience".

sections.label: Declaring voting results
sections.summary: The speaker declares 93 Ayes, three Noes and zero Abstentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.
